description: After the 2010 and 2011 Christchurch earthquakes, community-led temporary and adaptive urbanism filled a gap between emergency response and recovery, as citizens rethought how to rebuild and regenerate the city through collaborative processes and placemaking. This chapter assesses placemaking as a tool for post-disaster regeneration and resilience through three projects: the Re:START Mall, the Festival of Transitional Architecture (FESTA) and the placemaking programme at the Commons, and judges them against the Resilient Greater Christchurch Framework. A second candidate paper on transitional community-initiated open spaces in Christchurch (ResearchGate, blocked here) describes the same phenomenon and is matched to this record. Coverage: central Christchurch. Access: IntechOpen chapter. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-3.0. Caveats: qualitative assessment of a few projects. Simulation uses: representing interim public-space uses and community activity in recovery timelines. Related records: the Christchurch Central Recovery Plan Blueprint and the Great East Japan gathering spaces study.
